q: What is the main purpose of converting pyruvate to lactate in human muscle under anaerobic conditions?
options: To produce extra ATP from pyruvate when the mitochondria cannot be used
To oxidise reduced NAD back to NAD+, so glycolysis can keep making ATP
To release CO2, which keeps the pH of the muscle cells constant
To store energy as lactate for long-term use during later exercise
explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase transfers hydrogen from NADH to pyruvate: pyruvate + NADH + H+ → lactate + NAD+. No ATP is made in this step – its value is regenerating NAD+ for the triose phosphate oxidation step of glycolysis. Without it, NAD+ would run out and glycolysis, the only ATP source without O2, would stop.
